newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS - Svyazinvest sale seen delayed until June.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Svyazinvest sale seen delayed until June.

text.p: Russia will probably delay until next month one of this year's biggest state sell-offs -- the auction of a major stake in telecom holding company OAO Svyazinvest, a senior privatisation official said on Monday.

"I can't name a definite date now, but it won't be in May," Vladimir Malin, first deputy chairman of the Russian Federal Property Fund, told Reuters. "We're trying to do it as fast as possible -- I think it will be in June."

The government had planned to auction the 25 percent plus one share stake in mid-May, and hold an investment tender for a 24 percent stake at a later, unspecified date, as part of its privatisation programme this year.
But Malin said approval and registration of an increase in Svyazinvest's charter capital, called for in an government order dated May 23, could delay the auction.
"In order to conduct the auction, we have to carry out quite a few organisational procedures to register the new charter capital," he said. "Carrying this out could take up a certain amount of time."

The order, which set the starting price for the auction at $1.18 billion, called for the capital of Svyazinvest, which owns controlling stakes in 85 regional telecoms companies, to be increased by an unspecified amount through a new share issue.

The government has already ordered the transfer of state-owned stakes in four other companies -- long-distance provider Rostelekom, Tsentralny Telegraf, regional telecoms company Yekaterinburgskaya Gorodskaya Telefonnaya Set and telecoms consultants Giprosvyaz -- to Svyazinvest.

He confirmed that foreigners would be allowed to bid for the stake and that it would be sold as one unit, giving the holder power to block any changes to the charter of Svyazinvest, which holds controlling stakes in most regional telecoms.

Russia has been trying for about two years to sell the Svyazinvest stake. An earlier attempt to tender the 25 percent plus one share stake to strategic foreign investors, won by Italy's Stet Spa, subsequently fell through.
But the sale of the stake in Svyazinvest, one of Russia's largest companies, has become more and more pressing as worries over a huge budget deficit increase.

The government, currently battling with parliament over controversial budget cuts, has promised to find 30 trillion roubles ($5.2 billion) in emergency revenues from taxes from enterprises with the biggest tax arrears and from privatisation.

Malin said revenues from sell-offs this year of state stakes in national utility UES and oil holding company Rosneft, as well as the Svyazinvest sale and others, could be 10-12 trillion roubles ($1.7-2.0 billion) or more.
He said the sale of about 1.5 percent of the government's 52.7 percent stake in UES could be carried out through a share sale or through issuing convertible bonds.
He said it was possible the government, which plans to retain a 51 percent controlling stake, would wait until the end of the year to sell the stake.
The state has missed previous targets for privatisation revenues and sweetheart deals, where stakes in top companies are sold off at far below their market price, are common.
